conventions.convention: H is real L2 on [0,1] with its Borel sigma-algebra and restricted Lebesgue measure; elements are equivalence classes modulo null functions.

The m-approximation retains innovations at t through t-m+1 and replaces all earlier innovations using arrays mutually independent across time, approximation level and replacement index. Level zero replaces the entire input.
m-dependence means independence of the sigma-algebras generated by times at most a and times at least a+m+1, for every integer a.
The rank-one operator is (x⊗y)h = ⟨h,y⟩x; its product kernel is x(u)y(v). Covariance kernels are product-L2 equivalence classes, with no chosen pointwise representatives.
The finite-dependent vector CLT and Hilbert Gaussian construction assume AC and permit singular or zero covariance. The covariance-series lemma assumes Countable Choice and Dependent Choice.
The final CLT is weak convergence of Borel laws of normalized sums as single H-valued random elements; it asserts no convergence of time-indexed paths.

load_bearing.statement: A measurable causal Bernoulli shift is L2-m-approximable when E‖X0‖² < ∞ and the sum over m ≥ 1 of δm = ‖X0−X0,m‖L2(H) is finite, using the specified independent replacement arrays.

Under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, a centered L2-m-approximable causal shift has an absolutely trace-norm convergent long-run covariance series defining a positive self-adjoint trace-class operator Γ; its normalized-sum covariances converge to Γ in trace norm. The corresponding kernel series converges absolutely in product L2 and has integral operator Γ.

Assume AC. A centered strictly stationary m-dependent sequence of square-integrable real d-vectors, for finite d ≥ 1 and m ≥ 0, has normalized sums converging to Nd(0,Σm), where Σm is the sum of its lag covariances over |j| ≤ m and is symmetric positive semidefinite.

Assume AC. Every positive self-adjoint trace-class operator Γ on a separable real Hilbert space is the covariance of a Borel centered Hilbert-valued Gaussian random element, including finite-rank and zero covariance.

For a complete finite or countable orthonormal family in a real Hilbert space, the initial finite orthogonal projections converge in norm to each vector, and the squared-coordinate sums converge to its squared norm.
Independent centered, strongly measurable, Bochner-integrable square-integrable random elements in a real Hilbert space with a fixed complete finite or countable orthonormal basis satisfy E⟨U,V⟩ = 0.

Under Countable Choice, a real product-L2 kernel on [0,1]² defines a bounded operator on real L2 with operator norm at most its kernel norm; product kernels represent rank-one operators and satisfy the stated norm and inner-product factorizations.

Assume AC. For a centered L2-m-approximable causal Bernoulli shift in real L2([0,1]), n^(-1/2) times its first n sample sum converges weakly to a centered H-valued Gaussian with its long-run covariance Γ.
